absent: Object and page charge acquisition plus stock buffering and drain mechanics beyond offline draining and release discharge.
Full definitions, sizes and concurrency rules for control group, per node, vector and folio descriptors.
Reclaim iterator lifecycle and how positions guide scanning.
Statistics need detection, ratelimiting and propagation algorithms.
High limit enforcement, delay computation and batch sizing.
Generation sequence representation, increment routine and activity classification.
Legacy versus default hierarchy selection effects beyond state reparent gating.
Workqueue identities and scheduling contexts for deferred handlers.

findings.text: Offers adjustment of per node zone LRU occupancy for a given vector and list; requests are ignored while the controller is disabled, underflow is clamped to zero with a diagnostic, and accounting remains non negative.
Provides kernel memory counter adjustment for an address; untracked addresses affect only node counters while tracked addresses affect the owning group vector, resolved under read side protection.
Supplies three ways to obtain the vector lock for a folio with identical retry semantics and differing interrupt handling; ownership is revalidated after locking and acquisition restarts on mismatch.
Exposes lookup of the subsystem state for the group backing a folio, defaulting to the root state when hierarchy is off or when no group is associated.
Exposes numeric identifier of the nearest online ancestor group for the group associated with a page, returning zero when no online group exists.
Exposes referenced handle to the group of the current execution context, retrying acquisition when the reference cannot be taken and returning null while disabled.
Expose boolean checks that a statistic or event index lies within range and maps to a populated dense slot rather than the sentinel for unmapped entries.
Expose helpers to saturate per type generation counts for a node vector and to verify saturation still holds, used to prepare recipient state before migration.
Exposes migration of generation based folio organization plus traditional LRU size accounting from a donor vector to a recipient vector for one node.
Release assumes no live objects remain and that residual charged bytes are an exact multiple of page size; whole pages are discharged to the owning group before unlinking and deferred freeing.
Allocation yields a zeroed descriptor with empty list linkage and reference count wired to the release routine, or null when memory or reference initialization fails.
After transfer every queued object group is owned by the recipient and held on the recipient list, with no active entry left on the donor and the formerly active entry handed back for termination.
Dense index tables translate global statistic and event numbers to compact positions, using a sentinel for unmapped numbers and sizing derived from the listed item collections.
Event index construction covers fault, reclaim, swap, compression and migration families with conditional members, mapping each included global event to a dense slot and leaving others as sentinel.
Post migration combined donor plus recipient occupancy is unchanged with empty donor classes untouched and no double counting.

Post migration donor generation counters are zero while recipient counters reflect the combined total, folio linkage resides on the recipient side, and size class totals remain consistent with per generation activity flags.
Invalidation clears references to a defunct group from per node reclaim positions across ancestors, with an additional root pass when hierarchy is disabled and ancestry does not reach the root.
Non hierarchical state migration applies only on legacy hierarchy; one configuration flushes donor then recipient around local counter transfer, the other configuration performs no action.
Maximum sequence advancement requires successful per memory state progression when such state exists; success then permits increment of the vector maximum using the group swappiness bias.
Two feature gates for kernel memory accounting and BPF accounting start in the disabled position.

User visible memory breakdown associates display labels for kernel, file, anon plus slab, scan, steal, demote and workingset families with their underlying counters, including conditional entries for compression, swap, huge pages and promotion.

Node statistic collection spans LRU occupancy, slab bytes, workingset transitions, mapped and dirty state, writeback, shared memory, huge pages and scan steal demote refill activity, with conditional swap and promotion members.
Group only statistics cover kernel, socket, swap, per CPU and compressed swap byte and object counts.
Reparent acquisition follows fixed rank with the global object group lock outermost under interrupt masking, then donor vector lock, then recipient vector lock; release uses reverse rank.
Folio vector locking holds read side protection across lookup and acquisition and restarts the whole lookup when the vector owner no longer matches the folio owner.
Unlinking of a terminating object group occurs under the global object group lock with interrupt state preserved.
Sequence state progression for memory iteration is serialized by the associated list lock with single increment semantics guarded against going backwards.
Mutex object is defined for coordination of charge related paths; use sites are outside these fragments.

Per vector accounting uses a per CPU form holding current local values plus prior values for delta propagation, and an aggregated form holding subtree totals plus CPU only values plus pending child contributions, each sized by the node item count.

Group accounting uses a per CPU form with update counter, cached parent pointers, local state and event arrays plus prior arrays for propagation, aligned to avoid sharing, and a central form with aggregated, local only and pending arrays plus an atomic update counter, sized by combined state and event counts.
Per CPU charge cache holds a small array of group references with parallel page counts, plus deferred work, flag word and drain cursor, protected by a local try lock.

Per CPU object cache holds a small array of object group references with parallel byte remainders and slab byte adjustments, plus index, node identity, deferred work, flags and drain cursor under a local try lock; remainder width widens on very large page configurations.
Display table pairs human readable labels with statistic indices to render group memory breakdowns.
Object group lifetime moves from allocated with active references to killed with no new references and finally to released where residual pages are discharged and memory is freed after list removal.

Node reparent has a stable path that completes migration and donor termination and a retry path taken when recipient saturation lapses across lock acquisition, with voluntary rescheduling before reattempt.
Periodic statistics propagation remains continuously armed with a fixed delay and always performs full tree propagation rather than consulting the need indicator.
Deferred handler reclaims a fixed batch from the group owning the queued work using blocking allocation semantics.
Workqueue entry provides periodic full statistics propagation from the root.
CPU offline handler drains both object and page charge caches for the departing processor without extra locking.
Decrementing LRU occupancy below zero triggers a one time diagnostic and clamps the counter to zero, indicating accounting imbalance rather than silent wrap.
Residual object charges that are not page aligned trigger a one time diagnostic at release, since only whole pages can be discharged.
Group lookup from a page without stable reference is inherently racy and callers must tolerate transient association; offline groups are skipped toward ancestors under read side protection.
Locking a folio vector without revalidation risks operating on a stale group after migration; the retry protocol is mandatory for correctness.
Memory iteration sequence must never move backwards beyond the observed maximum; violation indicates lost update and is checked with a diagnostic.
Per CPU page cache capacity equals seven entries and per CPU object cache capacity equals five entries.
Statistics flush interval and maximum high delay each equal twice the kernel timer frequency.
High delay precision uses shift twenty and scaling uses shift fourteen.
Cached charge flushing marker equals zero.
Node item count derives from the length of the node statistic list and total state size adds the group only list length; event count derives from the length of the event list.
